elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT ... EXCEED ..." — the former TrueLink-only, Sections 3/4/7/11-limited cap now runs to both parties and to the Agreement as a whole, so Client's §12a indemnity exposure is inside an aggregate cap.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained basis is "TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), and the 12-month window is not anchored to the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No consequential/indirect damages exclusion appears in the rendered clause or elsewhere in the cited paragraphs; the drafter confirms none exists in the document and none was added.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out parenthetical: "(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, ...)" — mutual and unconditional.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out list names only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations carve-out.
"(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ...)" — applies to both parties' indemnities in §12a and §12b.
Carve-out includes "GROSS NEGLIGENCE" and is now mutual ("A PARTY'S"), replacing the TrueLink-only version.
Carve-out includes "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT", mutual as drafted.
Fraud does not appear in the carve-out parenthetical.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the rendered clause; the former Sections 3/4/7/11 scoping (which may have left IP matters uncapped) was replaced with an Agreement-wide cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language stating that Client's obligation to pay compensation/fees is not "damages" subject to the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT" — mutual and aggregate; no residual unlimited-Client-liability language remains (deterministic check confirms).

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — a 12-month fee-based measure, and hosting and support are the services this Agreement procures, so the basis is not illusory on its face.
"(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ...)" — mutual carve-out covering §12a and §12b.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" appears in the mutual carve-out parenthetical.
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE" retained in the carve-out and extended to either party.
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" retained in the carve-out and extended to either party.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single edited sentence delivers a mutual, aggregate, Agreement-wide cap on a retained 12-month fee basis with mutual carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct.

Minimality holds. Only the cap sentence was touched: party direction ("TRUELINK'S" to "EITHER PARTY'S"), scope ("SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT" to "THIS AGREEMENT") and the carve-out list. The scope broadening is necessary, not cosmetic: the indemnity sits in §12, which was outside the original 3/4/7/11 list, so without it Client's indemnity exposure would remain uncapped and the mutual aggregate-cap element would fail. The fee basis, amount and temporal anchor were left untouched; no survival tail, expense language or extra procedure was added.

Intent preserved: no cross-reference is left dangling (the section list was deleted, not orphaned), §12a/§12b indemnities continue to operate and are expressly carved out, and no retained sentence contradicts the new mutual cap.

Preferred level is not reached and should be offered as the opening ask if the negotiation allows: add the "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor, change "compensation paid" to "fees paid or payable", anchor the 12 months to "the event giving rise to the claim", add a mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion (none exists anywhere in the document), add carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP, and add that Client's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

Residual risk to confirm before sending (not a defect in the elements as drafted): the cap base is "compensation paid for hosting and support services". If the Agreement generates other consideration streams (e.g. per-report or transaction fees, set-up or licence charges), the base is a subset of total fees and the cap is narrower than 12 months' fees. If so, amend the base to "all fees paid or payable by Client under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim".

Drafting note: the carve-out for "A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" leaves Client's very broad §12a indemnity uncapped as well as TrueLink's §12b indemnity. That is the playbook position, but flag it in negotiation so the trade is deliberate.
